page: Microsoft Azure D2pls_v5 is an entry-level general purpose virtual machine powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. The instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz, configured with 1 thread per core. Memory capacity is 4.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage, requiring external persistent disks for file storage, and no discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results reflect the compact, low-memory ARM profile of the instance. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance falls in the average tier at 1822.08, while multi-core output reaches 3617.67, in the bottom 25% bracket. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 22.77 GB/sec for uncached read-only blocks and 14.05 GB/sec for write operations, placing memory bandwidth in the lower 10% bracket. Single-threaded gzip compression performs solidly at 24.13 GB/sec, whereas multi-core compilation and database operations register low throughput relative to larger cloud instances.

The hardware configuration provides high energy efficiency and predictable per-core performance via dedicated physical execution threads. However, the 4.0 GB memory footprint and lack of local scratch disks represent architectural tradeoffs, constraining performance under memory-intensive or heavy multi-threaded loads. The D2pls_v5 is primarily suited for lightweight web serving, low-traffic application backends, small Redis caching instances, and ARM development or CI/CD test runners.
description: Microsoft Azure D2pls_v5 is an entry-tier ARM-based general purpose virtual machine powered by an Ampere Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It features 2 dedicated physical cores, 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), and operates without integrated local storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its single-core compute performance in the average tier, with 1822.08 on stress-ng, while multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth fall into lower percentile tiers due to the dual-core, low-memory configuration. With no included local disk, workloads rely on remote storage solutions. The hardware profile offers steady per-core performance and strong power efficiency, making it cost-efficient for lightweight tasks. It is best suited for small-scale web servers, lightweight microservices, basic Redis caching, and ARM-native continuous integration and build pipelines.
